pronunciation.notes: Stress the an. The u is long, like the oo in 'food'.

intro.title: Ring ring
paragraphs: Your landlord's note says: Bitte rufen Sie mich an. You recognise rufen, and there's an an floating at the end of the sentence. Put them together and you get anrufen: please call me.
Anrufen is one of the first separable verbs most learners meet. Once it clicks, hundreds of other verbs follow the same rule.

etymology.title: Where it comes from

parts.note: The same an as in Ankunft.
Related to the old English word 'roop', a hoarse shout.

etymology.summary: Long before phones, anrufen meant calling out to someone. The telephone just took over the word.

bonus.note: Drop the -en and you get the noun. Der Anrufbeantworter, literally 'call answerer', is an answering machine.

tables.title: How it splits
tables.intro: In the present tense the an breaks off and goes to the end of the sentence. In the past it comes back, with ge squeezed in the middle.
notes: The … is where the rest of the sentence goes: Ich rufe dich morgen an.
In the infinitive and after a modal verb it stays in one piece: Ich muss dich anrufen.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: keeping it in one piece
keyTrap.explanation: In a normal sentence, anrufen splits. The rufen part takes second place and the an goes to the very end.

wrong.verdict: The an has to go to the end.

correct.note: Past: one word again, with ge in the middle.

correct.literal: I want you tomorrow to call.
correct.note: After will, kann, muss: one word at the end.

commonMistakes.title: dich, not dir
commonMistakes.explanation: You call someone directly, so the person is in the accusative: mich, dich, ihn, Sie.

commonMistakes.title: Calling a place
commonMistakes.explanation: To call a company, office or shop, use bei with the dative.
commonMistakes.correct: Ich rufe bei der Bank an.

commonMistakes.title: The past participle
commonMistakes.explanation: The ge goes between the two parts, never in front.

sampleSentences.german: Rufen Sie mich bitte morgen an.
Wann kann ich Sie erreichen? Ich rufe nach dem Mittagessen an.
sampleSentences.english: When can I reach you? I'll call after lunch.

sampleSentences.german: Ich muss noch beim Arzt anrufen.
sampleSentences.english: I still have to call the doctor's office.

quiz.fullAnswer: Ich rufe dich heute Abend an.
quiz.explanation: The verb part takes second place; an goes to the end.
Anrufen takes the accusative: mich, not mir.
The ge goes in the middle: an-ge-rufen.

quiz.prompt: How do you say "I'll call you back"?
quiz.explanation: Zurückrufen splits the same way as anrufen.
Rufe in second place, an at the end.

memoryHook: Anrufen is a phone call that hangs up early: the an always runs to the end. Ich rufe dich an.
